info.bio:
Kanye Omari West es un rapero y productor musical estadounidense nacido en Atlanta, Georgia, el 8 de junio de 1977, aunque creció en Chicago, Illinois, donde se mudó junto a su madre a la edad de tres años.

Tras asistir a la Academia Internacional de Arte y Diseño y Tecnología, una escuela de bellas artes de Chicago, y más adelante a la Universidad de Chicago, West abandonó todo y dio comienzo a su carrera musical. Ganó fama produciendo a artistas de rap y de R&B como Alicia Keys

own_scenes.desc: Hijo de la profesora de inglés Donda West, aprendió con No I.D. y Kyambo «Hip-Hop» Joshua lo llevó a Roc-A-Fella como productor: soul acelerado para Jay-Z, junto a Just Blaze. Nadie lo quería como rapero; al ver el documental Resurrection de Tupac entendió que podía «ser él mismo», y de ahí salieron el osito y el concepto de The College Dropout (2004). Rhymefest le pasó el «Walk with Me» del coro de un centro de rehabilitación: «Jesus Walks» («el verso es el pecado, el estribillo la salvación») ganó el Grammy. Producido casi entero por él, el disco, cuatro veces platino, apartó la violencia y el consumismo por la vulnerabilidad, la religión y la educación; Late Registration (2005) siguió con «Gold Digger», «Diamonds from Sierra Leone» y «Drive Slow» con Paul Wall. Luego vinieron las polémicas: «George Bush no se preocupa por los negros», Taylor Swift, Trump.

refs.q: I remember him saying, “I figured it out. I can be myself.”
refs.para: Roc-A-Fella was a last option. Basically, it was like we couldn’t get nowhere else—nobody was interested. Even with “Jesus Walks” and “Hey Mama.” They knew he could produce, but they probably thought that he was a producer-rapper. They didn’t see a big upside in that. The breakthrough moment came when we was watching Tupac’s documentary, Resurrection. I remember him saying, “I figured it out. I can be myself.” And after he said that, everything kind of clicked. The whole College Dropout concept came right after that. The whole four albums, the whole teddy bear mascot, all of that was probably like within a day or two of watching the Tupac film. He had a good three records at the same time, and that’s when he started getting taken seriously as an artist.

scenes.name: Jay-Z y Roc-A-Fella
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Shawn Carter aprendió con Jaz-O y recorrió las giras de Big Daddy Kane; DJ Clark Kent, convencido de que era «el Jesucristo del rap», dejó dos sellos que no quisieron ficharlo, le montó un estudio en casa y le presentó a Damon Dash, que defendía a su Big L. Con Dash y Kareem «Biggs» Burke fundó Roc-A-Fella (1995) para ser independiente. Reasonable Doubt (1996), rap mafioso de un buscavidas que reflexiona sobre esa vida («D’Evils», «Regrets»), con DJ Premier, Clark Kent, Ski Beatz («Dead Presidents», sobre Lonnie Liston Smith y una frase de Nas) y «Brooklyn’s Finest» con Biggie, que no podía creer que Jay no escribiera las rimas: se convirtieron en rivales y amigos. Iba a ser un solo disco; acabó con catorce números 1, Rocawear, la presidencia de Def Jam y el primer billón del hip hop. Roc-A-Fella, con Just Blaze, Kanye West, Beanie Sigel, Cam’ron, Memphis Bleek o Dipset bajo el mismo techo, se vendió a Island Def Jam en 2004.

podcast.title: Unauthorized Sampling Incident (2010)
podcast.body: Kanye West's 2010 song "Power" included an unapproved sample from King Crimson's first album. Robert Fripp was not informed prior to its release and learned about the sampling through public media in 2012. Universal Music, which owned West's label and held rights to the King Crimson material, retrospectively requested permission, but this failed to appease Fripp, leading to prolonged legal action. "sacaba un tema que se llama Power... usaba un sampling del primer tema de la primer disco de King Crimson y Robert Flip ni siquiera lo sabía."

podcast.body: Kenny West's famous Jesus tour in 2013 included Kendrick Lamar as a touring artist. This tour was significant as it was during this time that Kendrick Lamar's critically acclaimed album *To Pimp a Butterfly* began to take shape. "ya en el 2013 que va a de gira, con el propio Kenny West en su gira del Jesus tan famosa."

podcast.body: Kanye West engaged in a major dispute with Spotify and even created a competing streaming service, Tidal, to offer artists higher royalty payments. podcast.title: Catalyst for the "New School" of Hip Hop
podcast.body: Kanye West is credited with being the figure who connects classic rap with the truly experimental hip hop of the 21st century. His debut ushered in a "new golden age" where a diverse range of artists, inspired by his movement, revolutionized the genre. This led to a clear distinction in hip hop, with artists predating his debut often referred to as "old school" (e.g., Jay-Z, 50 Cent) and those influenced by him or emerging after, like Kendrick Lamar, Run the Jewels, and Death Grips, termed "new school." "Tenemos aquí justo en el medio la persona que conecta estos dos movimientos generales y de estilo que es el que es el mismísimo Kenny West."

"es que caniguo es y hace en el exacto lo mismo. Y si usted compra las sacan y modernas, tu te compra la MPC, la MPCX, todas las nuevas gama de la KMTC, es que sigan funcionando y trabajando exactamente igual que trabajaba de y eciado."

podcast.title: David Bowie Prediction Theory
podcast.body: A conspiracy theory suggests that David Bowie predicted Kanye West's rise to stardom in 1972, five years before his birth. Evidence cited includes the "K. West" sign on Bowie's *Ziggy Stardust* album cover, the song "Five Years" from that album, and the title of Bowie's final album, *Black Star*, which is interpreted as an "anointment" of Kanye as a "Black Star." Kanye West was also among the first to pay tribute to Bowie on Twitter after his death, and stories circulated about Kanye planning a Bowie tribute album. "David Bowie allegedly predicting the birth of Kanye West back in 1972, five years before it actually happened."

podcast.title: Industry Resistance to His Artist Career
podcast.body: Despite his strong reputation as a producer, the music industry was initially very reluctant to support Kanye West as an artist and promote his own material. This was primarily because his personal image — educated, well-dressed, articulate, and from an accommodated background (even studying fine arts at university) — did not fit the prevailing gangster rap profile of the mid-to-late 90s, which emphasized a delinquent, street-tough persona. "Toda la industria discográfica fue muy reacia desde un primer momento a trabajar en el propio material de Kenny West y a promocionarlo como artista."

podcast.body: Kanye is recognized as one of the artists who "really went to town with auto-tune," utilizing the technology not just for subtle pitch correction but for highly exaggerated and distinct vocal effects. His influential work contributed significantly to the trend of Auto-Tune being used as a deliberate stylistic choice in popular music. podcast.title: Pioneer of a New Hip Hop Image and Sound
podcast.body: Kanye West emerged as an artist challenging the dominant gangster rap aesthetic of the late 90s and early 2000s, which was exemplified by artists like 50 Cent, Jay-Z, and Eminem with their gold chains and tough attitudes. Kanye presented himself as well-dressed, well-spoken, and cultivated, with an exquisite vocabulary. His approach to hip hop was inspired by literature, establishing a more complex lyrical foundation that moved away from classic gangster rap themes. "Kenny West aparece justo en un momento en el que yo creo que todos estamos ya un poco cansados de esa imagen de 50 cent de Jay-Selt de Eminem incluso pues con sus caguenas y oro, con sus actitudes chulas que a con su mal educación, con sus líos, con sus armas y a veces Kenny West bien vestido, bien arreglado, un tío que habla bien, que tiene un vocabulario esquisito."

podcast.title: Rejection by Labels and Artists
podcast.body: Kanye West faced numerous rejections from record labels when trying to launch his artist career in the late 1990s, and even from artists he worked with, such as Jay-Z initially. He had serious discussions with Columbia Records, but they eventually backed out due to pressure from Roc-A-Fella Records, who did not want to lose him as a highly valued producer. "Lo único que consigues son negativas, negativas de las discográficas, pero también negativas a los propios artistas para los que trabajaba como en un principio el mismo J.S.E."

podcast.title: Transition from Producer to Artist
podcast.body: Before becoming a solo artist, Kanye West established himself as a highly significant producer in Black music, especially hip hop, starting in the mid-1990s. He worked with prominent artists like The Notorious B.I.G., Nas, and contributed to early Jay-Z albums, notably playing a major role in Jay-Z's resurgence with "The Blueprint." "Kini West empieza a trabajar a mitad de los 90 y muy rápido se convierte en un productor realmente importante en dentro de la música negra, principalmente el hip hop pero no solo del hip hop."

xref.title: Kanye West Prediction Theory
xref.body: A conspiracy theory claims David Bowie predicted the rise of Kanye West back in 1972. Proponents cite Bowie's *Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars* album (released June 16, 1972) and its song "Five Years" as foretelling the event, noting Kanye's birth on June 8, 1977, almost five years later. The theory also highlights the "K. West" sign visible on the *Ziggy Stardust* album cover (from a fur store), interpreting it as a direct reference, and Bowie's final album, *Black Star*, as an "anointment" of Kanye, referred to as a "Black Star." Bowie's known visionary capabilities regarding digital music, social media, and gender fluidity are used to support his ability to predict Kanye's ascendance. "Did David Bowie predict the rise of Kanye West way back in 1972?"
